messages:
mira_s: quick heads-up — canary for sparrow-lite-int8 is showing a spike in funcall JSON parse failures on the onboarding batch, ~0.9% vs 0.07% on float baseline. attaching short sample and logs. :thinking:
chen_w: ouch. can you paste the minimal repro and a sample output?
alex_g: is this from streaming responses or non-streaming? streaming often exposes suffix drops with kv-cache.
mira_s: streaming. repro steps:
  1) prompt with tool contract + short context (avg 120 tokens)
  2) model: sparrow-lite-int8, seq_len=512, kv_cache enabled, decode temp=0.0, topk=1 for canary
  3) sample rate ~1k requests over 6h

sample output (one failure):
```
Assistant: {"action": "create_ticket", "args": {"title": "User can't login", "description": "User reports 401 after oauth"}
...more tokens cutoff...
```

mira_s: logs show trailing token cutoff mid-json in 11/9 failures, others are malformed keys or extra commas.
chen_w: can you try with kv_cache disabled? also what quant pipeline used (per-channel/per-tensor, A/B)?
mira_s: used per-tensor symmetric int8 PTQ quick-pass. ran a small AB: per-channel reduced failures to 0.3% (still > baseline).
jules_r: my hunch—quant induced tokenization drift when logits at EOS boundary get lower probability, so streaming early-stop truncates JSON. try relaxing end-token threshold or add a sentinel end-of-json token in postprocess.
alex_g: pragmatic fixes: 1) increase retry budget from 1->3 with exponential backoff 150ms, 2) add a micro "json-wrap" postprocessor that wraps raw output in [ ... ] and attempts ndjson repair before feeding tools. both healed some %, but we need root cause for regression.
eval-bot: automated metrics for last run (6h window):
```
model,samples,parse_fail_rate,healed_by_repair
sparrow-float,1024,0.07%,N/A
sparrow-int8-ptq-per-tensor,1008,0.92%,12%
sparrow-int8-ptq-per-channel,1000,0.31%,28%
```

mira_s: noted. ran a focused non-streaming run — parse_fail_rate dropped to 0.05% for int8 per-channel. so streaming+kv seems necessary combo to trigger.
chen_w: any sign of k-v prefix truncation? earlier we saw suffix loss when cached prefixes change chunk boundaries.
jules_r: yeah, there's an odd case where cache re-use compresses prefix tokens and shifts later token alignments. quantized kernels might change exact token emission timing.

alex_g: proposed next steps:
- run targeted canary: int8-per-channel with kv_cache disabled (streaming on) and compare
- run int8-per-channel with kv_cache enabled but set "stream_chunk_size" smaller to force earlier flush
- add telemetry parse_error_type (truncation|malformed|extra_tokens) tagged to request_id
- temp increase retry budget for canary traffic and enable json-repair hook in postprocess

mira_s: I'll spin the two micro-runs now (should take ~3h). logging extra fields and sample dumps to s3:/canary/sparrow-lite-int8/2511123456/
chen_w: if we confirm kv+stream is the culprit, we should consider a runtime mitigation: automatic soft-close when model emits partial-struct signature (e.g., unmatched braces) and request a quick top-up decode before handing to tool.
jules_r: agreed — also add a canary that toggles quant kernel variant (fast vs compat) to see kernel-level differences.
alex_g: thanks — ping here with final numbers. if per-channel fixes it we can promote that quant profile as default for sparrow-lite. :rocket:
mira_s: thanks all, starting jobs. will post results and a 2-line summary when done. :white_check_mark:
